# Cadence plan report

Generated by `node test.mjs --report`. Every session from 15 to 60 minutes (recreational rates), measured as rowed and checked against the principles below.

## Principles

| ID | Principle | Source |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Range.** Every session runs from 15 to 60 minutes. | Product decision: one length range for every session. |
| P2 | **Shape.** The main set keeps its shape at every length: equal pieces differ by at most one coach step; pyramids rise then fall symmetrically; ladders descend within each climb. | Grammar rule 2. |
| P3 | **Growth.** Each length is a step of the session's single growth sequence, so a longer session is the shorter one plus more. | Grammar rule 3. |
| P4 | **Dose.** Hard minutes never decrease as the session gets longer. | Progression: more time means at least as much of the session's own work. |
| P5 | **Steps.** A growth step adds at most 5 minutes, so every stepper position has its own plan. Known exceptions are listed with their reason. | Stepper moves in 5-minute steps. |
| P6 | **Frame.** Warm-ups and cool-downs stay close to the library: warm-ups at most 8 minutes with no stretch of easy rowing over 4 minutes, cool-downs normally at most 5, and never over 8 when they absorb leftover time. | Dark Horse Rowing: 5 min warm-up and cool-down; RowAlong: 4 min warm-up; beginner guide: 5 min warm-up. |
| P7 | **Identity.** From 25 minutes, at least half the session is its own main set (work and the rests within it). | A session dominated by warm-up, cool-down or filler has become something else. |
| P8 | **Rest character.** Rests keep each session's character: short for sustained work, near equal for race pace, long for sprints. | Pete Plan: 3x10 min / 2 min, 8x500 m / 2-3:30 min; RowAlong: 10 x 1 min sprints / 2 min; Concept2 WOD pyramid / 1 min. |
| P9 | **Load.** Load (minutes x intensity weight) is reported for every plan; past "Best up to" a session is allowed to be more demanding than its references, and says so on its card. | Edwards-style intensity zones; reported, not a gate. |
